data.title: AI Workflow Startup Relay Shuts Down as Founder Joins Google’s Chrome Team
data.ai_summary: AI workflow automation startup Relay is shutting down, with founder and CEO Jacob Bank leaving to join Google as VP of Product for its Chrome team. This move aligns with Google's broader strategy to integrate AI capabilities into its core products, including the recently popularized Gemini app.

data.title: LinkedIn’s Connected Apps Let Workers Prove Real Tool Proficiency
data.ai_summary: LinkedIn launched a Connected Apps feature on June 18, 2026, that automatically pulls usage data from partner tools—including Descript, Duolingo, Lovable, Relay.app, and Replit—to generate verifiable skill summaries on user profiles, replacing self-reported skills with objective activity-based evidence. The feature addresses employer concerns about inflated resumes in a platform of 1.3 billion members experiencing 12 percent year-over-year revenue growth, with Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, and GitHub slated to join soon. The timing aligns with a surge in daily AI tool usage among U.S. employees and growing employer difficulty distinguishing real proficiency from keyword-stuffed profiles.
data.author: Ava Callegari

data.title: LinkedIn will tell others how you really use Adobe’s apps
data.ai_summary: LinkedIn launched a new "connected apps" feature on June 17, 2026, that allows users to link supported third-party applications to their profiles, with each app automatically generating specific descriptions of how the user actually utilizes it. The feature initially supports 19 apps, expanding to include 14 new integrations such as Buffer, Fiverr, HubSpot, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Github Copilot, and Zapier, with more promised "coming soon." The generated statements are uneditable by users and update in real time based on actual app usage, though LinkedIn plans to add notifications to alert users when their statements change.
data.author: Jess Weatherbed

data.title: LinkedIn adds more digital skills visibility

data.title: State of AI Agent Builders 2026: What 770 Verified G2 Reviews and 7 Leading Vendors Reveal
data.ai_summary: G2 published its 2026 State of AI Agent Builders Report analyzing 770 verified reviews and surveying seven vendors to assess buyer sentiment, vendor priorities, and market positioning in the AI agent builder category. The report found 91% of reviews are positive-leaning with an average 4.5/5 star rating, while vendors converged on orchestration as the central technical priority and identified API integration failures as the leading cause of workflow failures. The G2 Grid reveals the market remains unconsolidated with over 20 vendors competing in the high performers cluster, and the next 12 to 18 months will determine whether leadership consolidates or fragments further.
